title: The Power Jesus Walked In
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Jesus depended completely on the Holy Spirit, and the Father promises that same Spirit to everyone who asks.
exhortation: It's amazing. Jesus thought so highly of the Holy Spirit that he put him forward as the greatest gift he could give.

When I was younger, I had this thought in my mind that Jesus was just different because he was God. He had a power I don't have because he's God. Sure, Jesus could fast for 40 days and have a good attitude about it, because he's God. But as I read Scripture and got older, I realized that Jesus really did depend completely on the Holy Spirit. The power Jesus had on earth was the Holy Spirit. It wasn't some special power that we don't have.

That really helped me and changed me as I read Scripture. I saw Jesus being completely dependent on the Holy Spirit. The works he did, he did through the power of the Holy Spirit. So when he promises us the Holy Spirit, he's probably very excited to tell us. The Father has offered his Holy Spirit. God himself has offered himself for us. And that's the power in our Christian life.

Walking in the power of the Spirit is the goal we should have. It's how Jesus walked and did all the works he did. And it's how we can walk as well: in our struggle with sin, in our desire to share the gospel, to serve in the church, to raise children, to be a good husband or a good wife. The Holy Spirit is the power to do the things God has called us to do.

So as we worship and as we go through our day, let's remind ourselves that we don't need our own power. We don't need some special thing beyond the Holy Spirit. And we have a promise here: if we ask, it will be given.
prayer: Lord, just thinking of yesterday, when we talked about how your glory is made known in our weakness. That happens through the power of the Holy Spirit at work in our lives, in a posture of constant dependence on you. We do not trust in systems. We don't trust in having our ducks in a row, having the perfect order and everything figured out. What we need, Lord, is the Holy Spirit and everyday dependence on you, a posture in our hearts that knows that what you have called us to, you have also empowered us for.

So I pray that we would live this way, Lord God. Help us see moments and opportunities throughout our day where before we would have said, "This can't change. This relationship can't change. I can't be the evangelist I want to be or should be. I can't speak with my wife or my kids or lead the way I want to lead." But Lord, by the power of your Spirit, we have been given all we need for life and godliness and mission and purpose. So may we live dependent on your Holy Spirit. May we look to your example, Jesus, and follow it with a whole heart. In Jesus' name, amen.
